newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher, funds buy soyoil.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher, funds buy soyoil.

text.p: CBOT soy products posted modest gains Friday on fund shortcovering tied to a belief the week's sharp losses were overdone, pit sources said.

Reports soyoil basis levels in Brazil firmed dramatically were also deemed supportive. One cash trader said basis levels were quoted Friday at 20 cents under CBOT July futures, compared with 50 under on Thursday.

Weekly crush figures drew mixed reviews with some sources saying the lower-than-expected figure was bullish because it limited supplies while others said it implied demand was for soymeal was weakening.

National Oilseed Processors Association said U.S. soy crushings during the week ended May 14 totaled 23.457 million bushels. The market was expecting from 23.6 million to 25.1 million bushels. Last week's crush was 24,568 million bushels.

New crop gained on ideas cold weather, while not deadly to developing plants, could slow germination. Traders noted soil temperatures remained below normal so even early planted soybeans were not benefitting from the quick start.
Soymeal ended $3.70 to $2.10 higher, with July up $2.10 at $288.80 per ton. Soyoil settled 0.10 to 0.02 cent firmer, with July up 0.09 at 23.97 cents a lb.

On the day, funds were aggressive buyers of soyoil, led by Prudential Securities. Floor sources said Prudential bought 500 lots July. Refco Inc bought 200 December, Merrill Lynch bought 100 July and Dean Witter sold 600 December.
Commercials were also said to be buyers, including Cargill Inc with 200 lots July and 100 August, ADM with 100 July and Produce Grain with 200 July.
In soymeal, Cargill bought 300 July, Produce and Term Commodities each bought 100 July and Merrill Lynch bought 300 July, pit sources said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 27,293 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 15,000 lots, against Thursday's 17,010.
